hypotheses.title: Use declined public captures to reweight only source templates
hypotheses.result: Evidence appeared in 188 of 200 side histories from 100 old screening games, but no component posterior changed above 1e-12. Public facts had resolved or eliminated those components. Zero new tournament games; no strength claim.

hypotheses.title: Preserve an undisclosed Marshal or General when a disclosed actor has an equally good safe capture
hypotheses.result: Zero eligible choices in 356 fixed sampled roots from 48 old screening games, both colors. All 6,520 intervening baseline decisions reproduced. Even the same-victim alternative gate failed, so relaxing only exact score equality would not establish incidence. Zero new tournament games; no strength claim.

hypotheses.title: Redirect slow pursuers when a disclosed Scout can undo every quiet approach
hypotheses.status: deferred preflight: sparse later activation through persistent goal memory
hypotheses.result: In 356 sampled positions from 48 old screening games, the native veto changes all 14 certified Scout goals and zero immediate whole choices. A separate persistent forced-prefix test retains candidate goal memory: one later native choice changes among 6,520 decisions, eight own decisions after a veto. Goal memory differs for 47 decisions; all 6,520 public belief packets and RNG states match, and other strategy bytes do not differ. This is sparse activation on forced histories, without evidence of on-policy strength, permanent evadability or policy equivalence. No registered strength policy or new tournament follows.
